articles.title: DashLoc Launches DashDesk, an AI -Powered Customer Support Platform
articles.content: AI DashLoc Launches DashDesk, an AI-Powered Customer Support Platform ITN · September 1, 2026 · 3 min read Quick Summary New AI-powered helpdesk platform brings omnichannel customer conversations, automation and support operations into a unified workspace DashDesk enables businesses to streamline ticket management, improve response times and enhance customer experiences at scale Launch strengthens DashLoc’s integrated AI-powered MarTech ecosystem across… New AI-powered helpdesk platform brings omnichannel customer conversations, automation and support operations into a unified workspace DashDesk enables businesses to streamline ticket management, improve response times and enhance customer experiences at scale Launch strengthens DashLoc’s integrated AI-powered MarTech ecosystem across discovery, reputation, engagement and customer support Bengaluru, 01st September 2026: DashLoc, an AI-powered MarTech platform helping businesses strengthen their digital presence, customer engagement and online reputation, today announced the launch of DashDesk , an AI-powered customer support platform designed to help businesses manage customer conversations, automate support operations and deliver faster, more consistent experiences from a single workspace. As businesses engage with customers across multiple touchpoints, support teams often have to manage conversations through different platforms and systems. This can make it difficult to maintain context, track requests and ensure timely resolutions. DashDesk brings customer support operations together on a unified platform, enabling businesses to manage tickets, streamline workflows, collaborate across teams and gain greater visibility into customer interactions. Built with AI at its core, DashDesk combines intelligent automation with essential customer support capabilities. The platform enables businesses to manage customer queries through omnichannel ticket management , while features such as AI-assisted ticket routing, workflow automation, SLA management, knowledge base management, customer self-service portals, real-time analytics and CSAT tracking help support teams improve efficiency and consistency. By automating repetitive support processes and intelligently organizing incoming requests, DashDesk allows customer service teams to spend more time addressing complex customer issues. The platform is designed to help businesses reduce manual intervention, improve response and resolution times, and maintain a consistent support experience as customer interactions scale. DashDesk is built to support businesses across customer-centric sectors including retail, healthcare, BFSI, hospitality, automotive, education, telecom, aviation, real estate and e-commerce . Its scalable architecture enables both growing businesses and larger enterprises to manage increasing volumes of customer interactions while maintaining operational visibility. Commenting on the launch, Sumit Singh, Co-Founder & CEO, DashLoc, said: “Customer expectations around support have changed significantly. Businesses today need to respond quickly, maintain context across conversations and provide consistent service across channels. Yet, support operations are often spread across multiple systems, making it difficult for teams to work efficiently. With DashDesk, we are bringing these interactions into one intelligent workspace where AI and automation can take care of repetitive processes while teams focus on meaningful customer conversations. Our aim is to make customer support more connected, efficient and scalable for businesses as they grow.” The launch of DashDesk marks another step in DashLoc’s vision of building an integrated AI-powered platform covering different stages of the customer journey. articles.title: Odisha's Lok Bhavan becomes India's first Platinum certified green Lok Bhavan | Dailyhunt
articles.content: I n the heart of Bhubaneswar, the institution that has housed the Governor of Odisha since 1960 has earned a distinction no comparable campus in India holds. Advertisement Lok Bhavan, renamed from Raj Bhavan in December 2025, is now the country's first Lok Bhavan to receive IGBC Platinum green certification, and the first campus anywhere in India to reach Platinum under the stricter Green Campus v1 rating system introduced in July 2024. The final score was 88 out of 100, inside the Platinum band of 80 to 100 and among the highest rated green campuses in the country. Retrofitting a working campus The harder part is what it took to get there. Green certifications are easier to win on new construction, where efficiency can be designed in before the foundation is poured. Lok Bhavan is a functioning government campus with decades of built infrastructure, daily operations and public engagement running through it. Under Governor Dr. Hari Babu Kambhampati, the campus was assessed system by system. Civil works were carried out, electrical systems upgraded, water management strengthened, energy monitoring introduced, landscaping and irrigation reworked, and waste handling reorganised. Officials, engineers, consultants and stakeholders worked through a roadmap covering eight environmental and operational categories, with every credit evidenced. The category breakdown: site planning and management 23/25, sustainable transportation 7/7, water conservation 13/18, energy efficiency 17/18, material and resource management 8/8, health and well being 6/7, sustainable operation and maintenance 7/8, and innovation in design 7/9. Green cover, solar and water More than 80% of the campus remains under green cover. A biodiversity survey documented 2,374 trees across 72 species, with faunal records spanning 27 species and a Shannon Wiener diversity index of 3.59. A deer park sits within the grounds, alongside Atal Van, the ecological park dedicated to former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, where a T-55 battle tank and a Rafale model anchor a collection of defence and naval artefacts. On energy, the campus has installed 635 kWp of solar photovoltaic capacity, with major consuming systems metered and tracked. The Energy Performance Index stands at 50.57 kWh per square metre per year, positioning the campus as a candidate for net zero. Water saw the sharpest operational gain: more than 35% reduction in consumption. That came from an integrated rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge system built around recharge trenches, filter chambers, ponds and borewell recharge structures, combined with drip irrigation, controlled sprinklers, and separate monitoring of municipal supply, building systems, kitchen and irrigation lines. Waste is segregated at source. Organic waste from kitchens and landscaping is treated on site through vermicomposting, with 100% treatment and reuse, while the final review recorded 100% diversion of reported dry waste from landfill. The all electric carcade Lok Bhavan has also become the first in the country to adopt an all electric official carcade, backed by EV charging infrastructure and electric vehicles for internal movement.
